programs.title_tr: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Toz Metal Kusuru & Yere İndirmeler
programs.title_en: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Powder Metal Defect & Groundings
programs.current_status_tr: Yüksek basınçlı türbin disklerindeki mikroskobik toz metal kirliliği nedeniyle küresel çapta yüzlerce A320neo/A321neo uçağı planlanmamış motor bakımına alındı. Ortalama motor revizyon süresi (TAT) 250-300 günü buluyor.
programs.current_status_en: Contaminated powder metal in high-pressure turbine disks required accelerated inspections; hundreds of A320neo family jets grounded globally with MRO shop turnaround times reaching 250-300 days.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY filosundaki yaklaşık 30-40 adet A320/A321neo uçağı yerde bekliyor; kapasite açığını kapatmak için ıslak kiralama (wet lease) ve mevcut A320ceo uçaklarının hizmet ömrünü uzatma yoluna gidildi. Pegasus filosu ağırlıklı CFM LEAP motorlu olduğu için doğrudan etkilenmedi.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Turkish Airlines has 30-40 A321neo aircraft parked; capacity shortfall managed via wet leases and extending older A320ceo service lives. Pegasus remains largely unaffected due to CFM LEAP engine selection.
programs.timeline_horizon: 2026 yılı boyunca ve 2027 ilk yarısına kadar sürmesi bekleniyor.
programs.source_reference: RTX Corporation / FAA Airworthiness Directives (AD 2024-0044) / THY KAP Açıklamaları

programs.title_tr: Boeing 737 MAX Üretim Kısıtı (FAA Aylık 38 Tavanı) & Tedarik Zinciri
programs.title_en: Boeing 737 MAX FAA Monthly 38 Cap & Supply Chain Bottlecks
programs.current_status_tr: FAA'in kalite ve montaj denetimleri kapsamında Boeing 737 üretimini aylık 38 uçak tavanında tutması ve Spirit AeroSystems gövde teslimat gecikmeleri nedeniyle 2026 teslimat takvimleri 3-6 ay geriye ötelendi. MAX 7 ve MAX 10 sertifikasyonu gecikmeye devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: FAA capped 737 production at 38/month pending quality audit milestones; Spirit AeroSystems fuselage supply constraints pushed airline delivery slots back by 3 to 6 months. MAX 7 and MAX 10 certification remains pending.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: SunExpress ve THY teslimatları planlanan takvimin gerisinde seyrediyor; havayolları yoğun yaz ve sonbahar kapasite planlamalarını mevcut gövdelerle optimize ediyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: SunExpress and Turkish Airlines delivery streams experiencing slot postponements; carriers optimizing utilization on existing fleet assets.
programs.timeline_horizon: Aylık 38 üretim tavanının 2026 sonuna kadar aşamalı olarak artırılması hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: FAA Oversight Directives / Boeing Quarterly Deliveries / Airline Fleet Filings

programs.title_tr: Airbus A321XLR Ticari Teslimatları & Dar Gövde Uzun Menzil Devrimi
programs.title_en: Airbus A321XLR Entry into Service & Long-Range Narrowbody Wave
programs.current_status_tr: EASA tip sertifikasyonunu tamamlayan A321XLR, Iberia tarafından Madrid-Boston hattında ilk ticari uçuşlarına başladı. 4.700 deniz mili (8.700 km) menziliyle dar gövdede transatlantik ve kıtalararası uçuş maliyetlerini %30 düşürüyor.
programs.current_status_en: Having achieved EASA certification, the A321XLR commenced transatlantic operations with launch customer Iberia. Its 4,700 nm range unlocks thin long-haul routes at 30% lower trip cost.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Orta Doğu, Afrika ve ikincil Avrupa şehirlerine doğrudan bağlantı potansiyeli nedeniyle bölge taşıyıcıları tarafından yakından izleniyor. THY ve Pegasus filo stratejilerinde uzun vadeli alternatif.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Closely monitored by regional carriers for secondary point-to-point routes into Africa, Central Asia and Europe; potential long-term fit for Istanbul network.
programs.source_reference: EASA Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) / Airbus Commercial Aircraft Updates

programs.title_tr: Boeing 777-9 (777X) Test Uçuşları & Hizmete Giriş Tarihi
programs.current_status_tr: İtiş kolu bağlantı elemanındaki (thrust link) teknik arıza sonrası test uçuşları geçici olarak durdurulmuştu; Boeing ilk teslimat takvimini 2026 yılına (ve potansiyel olarak 2027'ye) revize etti. Başta Emirates ve Lufthansa olmak üzere amiral gemisi filoları A380 ve 777-300ER ömür uzatmak zorunda kaldı.
programs.current_status_en: Structural component inspection on engine thrust links required test fleet pause; initial deliveries rescheduled to 2026/2027. Major customers Emirates and Lufthansa forced to extend legacy 777-300ER and A380 service lives.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY'nin geniş gövde siparişlerinde Airbus A350-1000'e ağırlık vermesinde 777X gecikmeleri belirleyici stratejik etken oldu.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Delays were a primary catalyst for Turkish Airlines' decision to anchor its high-capacity widebody order book on the Airbus A350-1000.
programs.timeline_horizon: FAA tip sertifikasyonu ve ilk ticari teslimat 2026 sonu / 2027 hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: Boeing Defense, Space & Security / Airline IR Filings / Emirates President Statements

programs.title_tr: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Yüksek Basınç Türbini Dayanıklılığı & MRO Bekleme Süreleri
programs.title_en: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Hot-Section Durability & Shop Visit Backlogs
programs.current_status_tr: Sıcak iklim, tozlu hava sahası ve yüksek iniş-kalkış döngüsü altında çalışan LEAP motorlarında türbin kanatçığı erozyonu nedeniyle planlanandan erken motor indirme yaşanıyor. Küresel MRO atölyelerinde yedek parça ve motor kıtlığı devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: Harsh environment operations (heat, sand, high cycle utilization) causing premature hot-section turbine blade wear; global MRO shops experiencing parts constraints and extended turn-around times.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Pegasus'un filosunun belkemiğini oluşturan A321neo uçaklarında CFM LEAP-1A motorları kullanılıyor. Pegasus, proaktif motor rotasyonu ve yedek motor rezervasyonu ile uçak yerde kalma süresini (AOG) asgaride tutuyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Pegasus relies heavily on CFM LEAP-1A on its A321neo fleet; carrier leverages proactive engine rotation and buffer lease pools to keep AOG rates minimal.
programs.timeline_horizon: CFM'in güncellenmiş dayanıklı parça (durability kit) teslimatları 2026 boyunca yaygınlaşıyor.
programs.source_reference: Safran / GE Aerospace Engine Technical Briefings / Aviation Week MRO Watch

DUBAI, UAE, 05 November 2026: The Emirates Group today announced its half-year financial results, posting a profit before tax of AED 4.1 billion (US$ 1.1 billion) for the first six months of 2026-27, a remarkable performance against the disruption and high fuel prices caused by the ongoing conflict in the Gulf region. After accounting for income tax charges, the Group’s profit after tax is AED 3.6 billion (US$ 1.0 billion), down 66% from last year. Illustrating its strong operating performance, the Group achieved an EBITDA of AED 12.5 billion (US$ 3.4 billion), 41% lower than the AED 21.1 billion (US$ 5.7 billion) reported for the same period last year where the Group had set a new record for profit and revenue. Group revenue was AED 66.2 billion (US$ 18.0 billion) for the first six months of 2026-27, down 12% from AED 75.4 billion (US$ 20.6 billion) last year. The Group closed the first half year of 2026-27 with a cash position of AED 54.1 billion (US$ 14.7 billion) on 30 September 2026, compared to AED 59.6 billion (US$ 16.2 billion) on 31 March 2026. The Group has been able to tap on its own strong cash reserves to support business needs, including pre-delivery payments for aircraft and servicing existing debt obligations. The Group also paid the remaining AED 2 billion (US$ 545 million) in dividend to its owner, the Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD), of the AED 3.5 billion (US$ 953 million) declared for the financial year 2025-26. His Highness (HH) Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman and Chief Executive, Emirates Airline and Group said: “It has been a demanding six months, and once again our business model and our people stood up to the test. Against unprecedented regional challenges and high fuel prices, the Group has delivered a profit before tax of AED 4.1 billion (US$ 1.1 billion). Customer demand held firm and our cargo operations made a strong contribution, keeping revenue and cash levels healthy even as global jet fuel prices doubled against the same period last year, impacting our costs and profitability. “I’d like to thank the UAE government for its decisive response and its co-ordination of all stakeholders to enable the safe resumption of air transport in the aftermath of military activity across the Gulf region. The government’s measures have also led to the easing of travel advisories to and through the UAE. This has allowed us to restore our operations with confidence and to keep serving our customers and communities. “Throughout this time, we have not paused our investments. Emirates and dnata continue to commit significant resources to expand our fleet, enhance our products and services, and develop capabilities that will shape the future of our business. This is how we stay ahead and stay resilient to external challenges.” HH Sheikh Ahmed added: “We enter the second half of our 2026-27 financial year with measured optimism. While keeping a close watch on costs and geopolitical developments, we remain focused on delivering what Emirates and dnata are known for – safety, quality, and customer satisfaction. We’ve weathered challenges before, and with our strong cash position and solid foundation built up over the years, the Group is well-placed to navigate the headwinds of volatility and high fuel prices.” Compared to 31 March 2026, the Emirates Group’s employee base dropped by 2% to an overall count of 128,237 on 30 September 2026. However, both Emirates and dnata maintain ongoing recruitment drives to support business requirements. Emirates airline The first six months of 2026-27 brought significant challenges to Emirates’ operations as intermittent airspace restrictions and closures across the region tested the airline’s operational agility, while government travel advisories reshaped consumer choices and travel flows. During this period, Emirates focused on restoring its network and connectivity options through its Dubai hub. At 30 September, Emirates was operating 91% of its pre-disruption network, with its passenger and cargo network spanning 150 airports in 78 countries and territories. The airline also launched a series of initiatives to boost customer confidence, including an industry-first comprehensive travel cover that is unrestricted by government travel advisories, free date changes on booked tickets, and generous refund policies. Between 1 April and 30 September, Emirates expanded its inventory of Premium Economy seats and brought its latest cabin products to customers in even more markets, as it received delivery of 9 new A350 aircraft and completed the full cabin refurbishment of 12 aircraft (9 A380s, 3 Boeing 777s). Emirates’ retrofit programme , one of the world’s largest known such projects, represents a planned investment of over US$ 7.0 billion to bring Emirates’ latest cabin products across its fleet. The airline’s Starlink installation programme also continued at pace, equipping 36 more aircraft with high-speed Wi-Fi in the sky during the first six months of the year, and bringing Emirates’ total Starlink-installed fleet to 57 aircraft as of 30 September. To support its future fleet requirements, in May, Emirates broke ground on its US$ 5.1 billion engineering and Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) facility at Al Maktoum International Airport, with completion expected in the mid-2030s. Leading from the front even in testing times, Emirates launched two industry-first cabin products to rave customer reviews: the U-dream headrest built into Economy Class seats, and electronically controlled privacy dividers in Premium Economy . These innovations have raised the bar for Economy and Premium Economy travel, redefining comfort and privacy for customers in these cabin classes. On the ground, Emirates inaugurated the first of its new concept lounges in Munich, Frankfurt and Manchester, featuring the airline’s latest interior design palette and elevated services for premium customers and frequent flyers. Emirates also opened new travel stores bringing its total retail footprint over 30 stores, offering customers more personal and experiential service touchpoints. Emirates continued its efforts to make travel more inclusive with the roll-out of Travel Rehearsals at 15 more stations across the UK, Australia, Portugal, the Philippines, Madagascar and the Maldives in the first half of 2026-27. This successful programme, which has now run in 47 stations, supports young travellers with autism and their families, helping them build confidence and reduce travel anxiety via exposure to real-time airport and flight simulations. The airline also continued to make a positive impact on communities , working with partners to deliver CSR programmes across key markets. In the first half of the year, initiatives included: the opening of a renovated community tennis court in Miami as part of the Force for Good programme with the USTA Foundation; a refreshed youth technology and gaming room in New York City with NBA Cares; a new natural play area with the London Wildlife Trust as part of the Championing Nature programme with Wimbledon; and the launch of the Emirates Nourishment Programme to deliver 400,000 breakfasts annually to underprivileged kids across South Africa in partnership with EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation. During the first half of 2026-27, Emirates extended its successful and long-running sponsorship deals with Arsenal Football Club (until 2033), and with Real Madrid (until 2031), representing multi-year investments in global brand visibility and partnerships with two of the world’s most prominent clubs in football. Overall capacity during the first six months of the year decreased by 10% to 28.2 billion Available Tonne Kilometres (ATKM) due to a reduced flying schedule. Capacity measured in Available Seat Kilometres (ASKM), decreased by 17%, whilst passenger traffic carried measured in Revenue Passenger Kilometres (RPKM) was down by 25% with an average Passenger Seat Factor of 72.0%, compared with 79.5% during the same period last year. Emirates carried 21.8 million passengers between 1 April and 30 September 2026, down 22% from the same period last year. Emirates SkyCargo transported 1.2 million tonnes in the first six months of the year, down by 1% compared to the same period last year. However, cargo revenue increased by 52% as the regional conflict reduced available airfreight capacity while concurrently pushing shippers to seek airfreight options due to marine transport disruptions. In the first half of 2026-27, Emirates SkyCargo added capacity from 5 new Boeing 777 freighters delivered, and the deployment of its first passenger-to-freighter converted aircraft. The cargo division expanded its freighter network with two new destinations, Almaty and Zhengzhou; introduced dedicated freighter services to over 15 existing Emirates destinations; and increased frequencies to several key markets including in the Far East. Emirates profit after tax is AED 3.3 billion (US$ 903 million), down 66%. Emirates revenue , including other operating income, of AED 56.9 billion (US$ 15.5 billion) was down 13% compared with AED 65.6 billion (US$ 17.9 billion) last year. The airline’s revenue performance can be attributed to enduring travel demand across its markets, particularly for Emirates’ premium cabins, and a solid contribution from the airline’s cargo business. Gains of AED 7.1 billion from its fuel price risk management strategy significantly offset the impact of higher fuel prices, reducing the net fuel cost increase to 13%. Fuel remains the largest component of the airline’s operating cost at 34%. Emirates Flight Catering revenue from external customers declined by 51% to AED 273 million (US$ 74 million). Its uplift of 4.5 million airline meals was down by 41% due to reduced air traffic at Dubai’s airport during the period. Emirates Leisure Retail/MMI revenue declined by 13% to AED 1.2 billion, due to the impact of lower tourism traffic in the UAE during the first six months of 2026-27. dnata dnata’s airport operations, catering and retail, and travel services divisions adapted quickly to business and operating challenges caused by the regional conflict, with its international businesses helping to offset the impact of reduced airline and travel traffic in the UAE and the broader Gulf region. In the first half of 2026-27, dnata continued to win customers with its safe and high-quality services across its global operations, signing multi-year agreements, including a cargo partnership with Silk Way Group in Singapore and inflight catering contracts with Cathay Pacific across several airports in the UK and the USA. Notably, dnata Airport Operations secured a seven-year ground handling license at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport, reinforcing its position at one of Europe’s key aviation hubs. dnata continued to make strategic investments to grow its capabilities and enhance its customer offering. In the first six months this year, dnata opened a new integrated command centre to support its growing cargo operations in Dubai; committed to an AED 8 million investment to expand The Fort – Lisaili, Arabian Adventures’ desert tourism destination in Dubai; and continued to invest in advanced technology and equipment across its operations including automated aircraft approach systems in Dubai, an aircraft catering simulator in Dublin, and autonomous tractor trials in Europe and Asia. In addition, dnata announced an AU$ 32 million investment to build a new cargo facility at Western Sydney International Airport (WSI), while construction of its new catering facility at WSI is on track for a 2027 opening. It also continued to deliver its global cargo and logistics strategy through targeted investments across its network, commissioning its new AED 100 million (US$ 27 million) logistics facility in Dubai South and progressing strategic developments, including a planned AED 37 million investment in Alat, Azerbaijan, alongside new and expanded cargo operations at East Midlands Airport and Zurich Airport. In its Travel division, dnata integrated its Imagine Cruising and Travelbag businesses, bringing together two complementary portfolios to build greater scale, share expertise, and drive international growth. dnata’s revenue , including other operating income, reached AED 11.0 billion (US$ 3.0 billion) down by 7% compared to AED 11.7 billion (US$ 3.2 billion) generated in the same period last year. stories.lead: European flight volumes fell to an average of 32,480 daily flights due to adverse weather and reduced capacity across major operators. Despite the weekly dip, overall network traffic remained 0.7% higher than the corresponding week in 2025.
stories.source_description: The network averaged 32,480 daily flights (including overflights), down 2.3% from Week 42 and 0.7% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Storms Austen and Boelo caused widespread flight disruptions across northern and western Europe between 23-25 October 2026. Flight volumes across the 10 busiest States fell by an average of 2.5% with none recording growth. Greece saw the most significant decrease (-7%). Network arrival and departure punctuality were 73.5% and 69.4%, better than in the equivalent week of 2025. Total air traffic flow management (ATFM) delay was 2.4 min/flight (1.7 for en-route and 0.7 for airport). ATC capacity & staffing was the top delay cause (65% of all en-route ATFM delays), followed by weather (20%).

stories.lead: Boeing forecasts that the global commercial aircraft fleet will grow nearly 80% to over 50,000 airplanes by 2045. Airlines and cargo operators will require nearly 44,000 new aircraft over the next 20 years to support air travel and cargo expansion.
stories.source_description: The global commercial airplanes fleet is expected to grow nearly 80% to more than 50,000 airplanes by 2045 as airlines and cargo operators add capacity. Globally, operators are forecasted to need nearly 44,000 new airplanes to support sustained air travel demand and air cargo expansion over the next 20 years. stories.headline: Emirates Brings the NBA Experience Onboard with Special Menus and Basketball-Themed Offerings
stories.lead: Emirates is launching a basketball-themed inflight experience on select flights to the U.S. and Canada to celebrate the 2026/2027 NBA season.
stories.source_description: New York, US – 06 November 2026: Emirates, the Official Global Airline Partner of the NBA, is bringing the excitement of basketball to the skies with a special NBA-themed inflight experience, available until 23 November 2026. Customers travelling on select Emirates flights to the U.S. and Canada can enjoy basketball-inspired menus, themed cabin touches and a curated selection of sports entertainment, celebrating the season tip off and the airline’s global partnership with the NBA. Customers travelling across all cabins will discover special NBA-themed touches designed to bring the spirit of the game onboard. Premium Economy and Economy Class customers will find co-branded cabin elements, including NBA-themed headrests and custom beverage coasters, adding a courtside-inspired touch to the inflight experience. The special inflight offering features a range of basketball-inspired dishes and refreshments. First Class customers can enjoy delectable themed desserts like chocolate and hazelnut cookies, topped with caramel sauce and served with ice cream, while travellers in Business Class and Premium Economy will savour chocolate cheesecake with sour cherry compote. Customers seated in Economy Class will finish their meals with salted caramel milk cake. Emirates is bringing fans together over their shared passion for basketball with special court-side fare and snacks, including Margherita pizza and beef hotdogs delivered direct to passengers travelling in Premium Economy and Economy Class. First Class and Business Class customers flying on Emirates’ iconic A380 aircraft can get into the NBA spirit at the Onboard Lounge, indulging in crispy chicken tenders with buffalo sauce, macaroni and cheese and a selection of mini bistro bites on select flights from Dubai. On flights from US and Canadian points to Dubai, the celebrations continue at the A380 Onboard Lounge, with a menu featuring lemon drizzle bundt cake and toffee apple and pecan crisp bundt cake. Customers visiting Emirates’ lounges in Dubai can also enjoy a selection of NBA-inspired food and beverages. The First Class Lounge will feature the NBA Signature Wagyu Burger, served with Rocca leaves, pear and bacon jam, fries and salad. Guests can also enjoy themed beverages, including the Pick and Roll cocktail and Step Back Cooler mocktail, alongside a selection of desserts such as passion fruit tart, a milk chocolate and coconut sphere, and pistachio éclair. In the Business Class Lounge in Dubai, customers can enjoy a live nachos station, a corn dog station, themed cocktails and mocktails, and a selection of desserts. Customers visiting Emirates lounges in Boston, New York, Los Angeles and San Francisco can also enjoy specially curated menus inspired by the local basketball teams, with dishes celebrating the Boston Celtics, New York Knicks, Los Angeles Lakers and Golden State Warriors. Onboard, basketball fans can also enjoy a curated selection of sports entertainment through Emirates’ award-winning inflight entertainment system, ice. The TV sports category features more than 30 titles, including Running Point and Game 5 of the 2024 NBA Finals between the Dallas Mavericks and Boston Celtics. The movie sports category features more than 60 films and documentaries, including Jerry West: The Logo , Warrior Strong and Finding Tony . NBA-themed welcome screens, animations and other inflight entertainment touchpoints will further bring the partnership to life. The limited-time NBA experience reflects Emirates’ commitment to delivering premium experiences for customers both in the air and on the ground. Now in its second year of activation since the partnership launched in 2024, the collaboration reinforces Emirates’ connection with basketball fans around the world, bringing the excitement of the game to customers as they travel. Today, we fly the world’s biggest fleets of Airbus A380s and Boeing 777s, offering our customers the comforts of the latest and most efficient wide-body aircraft in the skies. We inspire travellers around the world with our growing network of worldwide destinations, industry-leading inflight entertainment, regionally inspired cuisine, and world-class service.

stories.headline: Emirates Launches Nourishment Programme for South African Youth
stories.lead: Emirates, in partnership with EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation, has initiated a long-term programme to support children in South Africa through nutrition and education.
stories.source_description: More than 800 Cape Town primary school students took part in a day of nutrition, rugby, education and creativity as part of the Emirates Nourishment Programme Emirates, EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation were joined by DHL Stormers players including Siya Kolisi to inspire children through rugby, teamwork and positive role models The long-term programme aims to support 2,000 children every year across Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban, helping them overcome barriers to learning and reach their potential Cape Town, South Africa, 4 November 2026 – More than 800 primary school students in Cape Town enjoyed a day of rugby, learning and creativity as Emirates, European Professional Club Rugby (EPCR) and the Kolisi Foundation brought the Emirates Nourishment Programme to life at a local school. Joined by DHL Stormers players, Kolisi Foundation founder Siya Kolisi, Emirates Cabin Crew and team members from South Africa and Dubai, and EPCR representatives, the partners showed how good nutrition, education and the power of sport can help children build confidence and realise their potential. stories.headline: SWISS to Deploy Airbus A350-900 on Zurich-Mumbai Route

The entirely redesigned cabin offers greater comfort and privacy, along with state-of-the-art entertainment systems featuring larger screens. Its lighter construction, more powerful engines and higher cruising altitude all contribute to the shorter flight time. “SWISS Wanderlust” to remain in the skies longer SWISS will keep the special “SWISS Wanderlust” livery on its first Airbus A350 longer than originally planned. The airline initially intended to retain the elaborate design until the first quarter of 2027 but has now decided to extend its use beyond that period. SWISS has not yet determined how long the aircraft will continue flying in its special livery. The airline plans to restore the classic SWISS livery during an already scheduled repainting. SWISS embodies Switzerland’s traditional values and is dedicated to delivering the highest product and service quality. The company also helps drive the decarbonization of the airline sector by modernizing its aircraft fleet, using sustainable aviation fuels and bringing ever greater efficiency to its operational processes. Our largest business segment is Passenger Airlines while other key business segments include Logistics and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO). Other companies and Group functions such as IT companies and Lufthansa Aviation Training form complementary components of the Group. All airlines and business segments play leading roles in their respective markets.

stories.headline: Emirates Announces Australian-Inspired Theme for Australian Open 2027 Sponsorship
stories.lead: Emirates has unveiled its plans for the Australian Open 2027, highlighting a 30-year history of operations in Australia and an expanded tournament schedule.
stories.source_description: Australian-inspired theme brings the best of the country to life through food, entertainment and design at Emirates’ Marquee. Kids Tennis Day Presented by Emirates moves to Sunday, 10 January as the Australian Open expands to 22 days and the Rod Laver Arena Spectacular returns. MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA, 6 November 2026 – Emirates today announced an Australian-inspired theme for its presence at the Australian Open (AO) 2027, marking more than 30 years of connecting Australia to the world. The announcement comes as Tennis Australia revealed that this year’s tournament will expand into a 21-day experience, with Kids Tennis Day Presented by Emirates moving to Sunday, 10 January 2027 – giving families even more opportunities to be part of the action at Melbourne Park. The Emirates Marquee: A celebration of Australia at Melbourne Park The exclusive Emirates Marquee at AO will showcase Australian culture, food and entertainment, celebrating more than 30 years of the airline connecting Australia to the world. Inspired by the beauty of the Australian coastline, the Marquee’s “Coastline as a Landscape” design translates the sea, sand and sky into an abstract, sophisticated form. Layered horizontal curves and a natural palette will create a sense of calm, movement and timeless luxury – distinctly Australian, while remaining unmistakably Emirates. The 2027 menu, “Adventures Around the Coastline”, celebrates Australia’s rich and diverse food culture, showcasing the produce, flavours and traditions shaped by the country’s vast landscapes and varied climates. Guests will take an “adventure around the coastline”, from Mount Martha mussel escabeche and paperbark-smoked salmon to quandong-cured kingfish and seasonal shucked oysters, alongside Indigo Valley lamb with a Vegemite glaze and a pavlova station topped with Davidson plum meringues. Australian classics will also be reimagined with a touch of theatre, including “Adult Fairy Bread” – petite toasts topped with premium roes, built in front of guests – and “Shrimp on the Barbie”, smoked under cloche and brushed with charcoal oil to recreate that iconic barbecue flavour. Emirates’ famous unlimited First-Class caviar service returns, served at selected events and throughout the Finals Series. The airline will host more than 1,350 guests in the Marquee throughout AO27, including Skywards members, global business leaders, celebrities and sporting icons, building on more than 16,000 guests welcomed since 2015. Barry Brown, Divisional Vice President Australasia at Emirates , said: “For more than 30 years, Emirates has been connecting Australia to the world, and the world to Australia. As we return as Official Airline of the Australian Open for 2027, it only felt right to put Australia at the centre of it all. “Our AO27 theme is a celebration of everything we love about Australia - its food, its creativity and its world-famous hospitality - brought together with the signature Emirates experience. We're also proud to continue presenting Kids Tennis Day Presented by Emirates, and to help even more young Australians fall in love with the game.” Andrew Abdo, CEO of Tennis Australia , added: "The Australian Open continues to evolve and 2027 marks another exciting milestone as we expand to a 22-day tournament for the first time. By moving Kids Tennis Day to Sunday 10 January, we're creating an additional day for fans to enjoy everything the AO has to offer while putting families and young people at the heart of the tournament's opening weekend. Australian tennis legend Lleyton Hewitt said: “Kids Tennis Day Presented by Emirates gives kids and families the chance to get up close to the game, have some fun and be inspired by tennis’ biggest stars. These experiences can spark a lifelong love of tennis, whether it’s picking up a racquet for the first time or taking the next step in the sport. Having Kids Tennis Day kick off the Australian Open this year is a fantastic outcome for families and a great way to start the tournament.” Engaging Fans on the Ground and in the Sky Emirates will once again connect with tennis fans of all ages across Melbourne Park. Kids Tennis Day Presented by Emirates will now take place on Sunday, 10 January, with exclusive one-day-only activities across the precinct and the return of the popular Rod Laver Spectacular. The airline’s commitment to connecting fans begins in the air, with matches aired live on the award-winning inflight entertainment system ice and special AO-themed amenities and menus onboard.

stories.headline: Emirates Celebrates Diwali with Special Menus Across Nine Indian Destinations
stories.lead: Emirates is celebrating the Diwali festival by offering traditional Indian sweets and festive dining experiences for passengers traveling between Dubai and nine Indian cities on 7 and 8 November 2026.
stories.source_description: Dubai, UAE, 4 November 2026: Emirates is bringing the sparkle and spirit of Diwali to the skies, celebrating the Hindu festival of lights with traditional Indian delicacies, festive dining experiences and a world of entertainment. On 7 and 8 November, customers travelling between Dubai and nine Indian destinations - Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Kochi, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Thiruvananthapuram, Kolkata and Mumbai, can enjoy special Diwali sweets across all cabin classes while select Emirates lounges will serve an array of Indian favourites to mark the occasion. Traditional Diwali sweets served across all cabin classes Emirates customers travelling to and from India can enjoy a taste of Diwali with traditional Indian sweets served onboard. Premium Economy and Economy Class customers will be treated to motichoor laddu alongside their hot meal - delicate, golden chickpea flour pearls soaked in sugar syrup, infused with fragrant cardamom and saffron, and finished with pistachios. First and Business Class customers can also indulge in kaju pista roll , a rich, rose-flavoured confection made with cashews, pistachios, dried fruits and nuts, elegantly wrapped in edible silver leaf. Festive Indian cuisine and Diwali desserts in Emirates’ First and Business Class Lounges From 3 to 8 November, Emirates’ First and Business Class Lounges in Dubai will celebrate Diwali with a vibrant selection of Indian specialities. Customers can savour vada pav accompanied by tangy tamarind and refreshing mint chutneys, followed by an assortment of traditional desserts including malai sandwich , mango delight , malai roll and the much-loved gajar ka halwa . First Class customers can also raise a toast to the festivities with a specially crafted Spicy Saffron Martini or a refreshing Iced Masala Cooler mocktail. In Emirates’ Business Class Lounges in Dubai, the festive menu will feature savoury favourites including vegetable keema samosa , onion kachori and paneer potli samosa , served with tamarind and mint chutneys. For a sweet finish, customers can enjoy balushahi , mango rajbhog and mini kesari rasgullas . The celebrations will extend to Emirates’ lounges in Cape Town and Johannesburg, where customers can enjoy an assortment of traditional sweets including coconut ice , barfi and jalebi . Bollywood blockbusters, Indian TV and music on ice The Diwali celebrations continue onboard with a rich selection of Indian entertainment on Emirates’ award-winning inflight entertainment system, ice . Customers can choose from up to 157 Indian movies, including Bollywood titles such as Mardaani 3 , Mayasabha – The Hall of Illusion and Coolie , alongside a wide range of regional films in nine languages – Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi, Punjabi, Bhojpuri, Bengali and Gujarati. For those who prefer the small screen, ice offers 14 Indian TV programmes, including Pritam and Pedro , Looteri Dulhan and Crime Patrol - 26 Jurm, 26 Cases. Music lovers can also set the mood for the festivities with a selection of 40 Indian albums and playlists, bringing the sounds of Diwali to the skies. Read more

Lufthansa Cargo tripled its operating profit to 162 million euros, while Lufthansa Technik increased its result by more than 50 percent to 200 million euros.
Network airline unit cost increases were limited to half a percent through moderate growth and strict cost management.
